# Purpose

Award credit for a defensible cutter/holder load path, a fixed-end cantilever idealization, correct moment and torque resultants, consistent millimeter-newton units, co-located bending and torsional stress components, correct von Mises and factor-of-safety calculations, and an engineering conclusion bounded by the model.

# Source and Input Distinctions

Suraidah et al. (2020), “End milling finite element method for cutting force prediction and material removal analysis,” *IOP Conference Series: Materials Science and Engineering* 788, 012020, DOI 10.1088/1757-899X/788/1/012020 (CC BY 3.0), supports the Aluminum 6061 end-milling context, the 10 mm HSS cutter, and measurement of radial, tangential, and axial cutting-force components. Detailed machining settings are background context only and are not student calculation inputs.

The transverse force of 15 N and tangential force of 10 N are representative physically reasonable light-cutting design loads, not exact experimental readings. The 30 mm effective overhang is an instructor-selected modeling value, giving <em>L</em>/<em>D</em> = 3 for the baseline cutter. The 1263 MPa yield strength is a published representative value from Sandvik Osprey heat-treated M2 data at approximately 66 HRC; it is a separate material-property basis and is not claimed as the verified material condition of the Suraidah cutter. The required static factor of safety of 2.0 is instructor specified.

The industry image attribution is provisional. The faculty template identifies a visually matching Wikimedia Commons record, “Roughing Endmill in Use.jpg” by David English (Fixerdave), CC BY-SA 4.0, but requires exact file/version confirmation before public release.

# Scope of the Base Problem

Use a prismatic solid circular cantilever fixed at the holder face, static end loads replacing time-varying tooth contact, linear elasticity, and small deformation. Exclude flute-root stress concentrations, helical geometry, interrupted cutting, runout, chatter, fatigue, wear, thermal effects, local cutting-edge failure, and detailed tool-life prediction.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and load path: 20%;
- idealization and assumptions: 20%;
- resultants, stresses, von Mises stress, and factor of safety: 40%;
- sensitivity and bounded engineering interpretation: 20%.
